notes: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, 'Evaluation of Thermal Control Coatings and Polymeric Materials Exposed to Ground Simulated Atomic Oxygen and Vacuum Ultraviolet Radiation', NASA TP-3595 (1995). Figure 3 caption: 'DK2 and LPSR reflectance of AODTS-exposed black duranodic anodized aluminum.' Read off the graph at 1000-1064 nm: about 0.11-0.12 with the Beckman DK2 and about 0.17-0.20 with the AZ Technology LPSR (pre- and post-exposure curves); the curves rise from about 0.05-0.10 in the visible to about 0.30-0.45 at 2500 nm. Instruments, in the paper's words: the DK2 'was used ... to measure diffuse reflectance from 200 to 2,500 nm. This instrument uses a 20.3-cm (8-in) diameter integrating sphere coated with magnesium oxide in which the sample is centrally located'; the LPSR 'measures diffuse reflectance from 250 to 2,500 nm using a 10-cm (4-in) diameter integrating sphere'. Table 1: solar absorptance 0.82-0.89, IR emittance 0.88. CAVEAT: Duranodic is an integral-colour hard anodise, not the common dyed Type II black; Anoplate's chart (see CL60/CL65) shows dyed black anodise rising to about 29% above 700 nm, so dyed black is likely worse at 1064 nm.
